passages.where: A worshiper asks what offering could satisfy God, thousands of rams or rivers of oil, and the prophet answers that God has already shown what is good: to act justly, to love mercy and to walk humbly with him. The site's note says the prophets attacked worship cut off from justice, though they did not abolish worship itself. Mercy here is something to love, not only to do now and then.

A Samaritan sees the beaten man, has compassion, binds his wounds with oil and wine, brings him to an inn and pays for his care in advance. The site's note says he takes on open-ended responsibility for a stranger, and the plain note says the question becomes whose neighbour you are willing to be. The lawyer cannot bring himself to say the Samaritan; he says, the one who showed him mercy.

Boaz tells Ruth, a foreigner gleaning in his field, that he has heard all she has done for her mother-in-law, and asks the LORD to reward her, under whose wings she has taken refuge. The site's note on the chapter says he protects her, feeds her and quietly tells his workers to leave extra grain for her. His kindness began with noticing, and much of it was done without her seeing.

David seeks out Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, lame in both feet, tells him not to be afraid, restores his grandfather Saul's land, and gives him a place at the king's table for Jonathan's sake. The site's note gives two readings, one suspicious of David's motives and one that takes the narrator at his word that he is keeping faith with Jonathan. Either way, Mephibosheth ate at the king's table for the rest of his life.

Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and he will repay the lender. The site's note says the chapter returns again and again to the poor, and that Proverbs never offers laziness as the only reason for poverty, naming injustice, oppression and plain misfortune as well. God counts what is given to the poor as given to him.

A righteous man regards the life of his animal, but the tender mercies of the wicked are only cruelty. The site's note lists care for animals among the chapter's subjects. Kindness reaches even to creatures that cannot thank anyone.

Moved with compassion, Jesus reaches out and touches the man with leprosy and says, I am willing; be clean. The site's note says that in touching an unclean person Jesus does not become unclean; the cleanness moves the other way. The plain note says the man doubted not Jesus' power but his wanting, and Jesus answered that first.

After the shipwreck, the islanders of Malta show Paul's company extraordinary kindness, lighting a fire and welcoming them all because it was raining and cold. The site's plain note says they had no knowledge of Israel's God, and asks whether we have ever been surprised by the goodness of people outside our faith and thanked them. Kindness is something to receive humbly as well as to give.

Paul asks the one who judges others whether he despises the riches of God's kindness, tolerance and patience, not realizing that God's kindness leads him to repentance. The site's note says God's kindness is not indifference to sin but time given for repentance. Kindness, in God's hands, is how hard hearts are turned.

Paul says that when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared, he saved us, not by righteous deeds we had done but according to his mercy. The site's plain note asks whether we remember what we were before grace found us, and how that changes the way we see others. All human kindness in Scripture answers a kindness that came first.

misread.taken: Clothe yourselves with compassion and kindness, and forgive as the Lord forgave you, is used to tell a badly hurt person to act as if nothing happened, keep being nice, and go back to someone who is still hurting them.
misread.says: The site's plain note answers that question with a plain no. Forgiveness lets go of revenge; it is not the same as trusting someone again, and it does not mean a crime should go unreported or that anyone should stay in danger. A person can forgive and still keep a safe distance and tell the truth about what happened, and nothing in the passage asks anyone to stay where they or their children are in danger.

whole: Kindness can sound small beside the great words of faith, a lesson for children. Yet most people can name the kind act that kept them going in a bad year: a meal left on a doorstep, a teacher who noticed, a stranger who stopped. Many of us are kind to people who can return it and short with those who cannot, gentle in public and sharp at home. Some confuse kindness with never saying anything hard, and others think being honest gives them the right to be unkind.

Scripture puts kindness much higher than that. Micah sums up what the LORD requires as acting justly, loving mercy and walking humbly with God. Paul says it is God's kindness that leads a person to repentance, and that the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared when he saved us, not by our deeds but by his mercy. Kindness in the Bible is first something God does, and only then something he asks. Part of why we are not kind is that we are tired; part is that we decide who deserves it. The lawyer in Luke wanted to know who counted as his neighbour, and Jesus answered with a Samaritan, a man the lawyer could not bring himself to name. Most of us have someone we were raised to look down on, and the parable makes that person the one who did right.

So the Bible's wisdom about kindness is practical. It notices, as Boaz noticed Ruth's loyalty and quietly told his workers to leave grain for her. It remembers old debts of love, as David looked for someone in Saul's house to whom he could show kindness for Jonathan's sake. It reaches the poor, since Proverbs calls kindness to them a loan to the LORD, and it reaches even an animal. It touches what others avoid, as Jesus touched the man with leprosy. And it receives kindness humbly, as Paul's shipwrecked company did from islanders who knew nothing of Israel's God. Kindness is not the same as having no limits: the site's plain note on Colossians 3 says that forgiving and bearing with one another never means staying where someone is hurting you, and the Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

The hope Scripture gives is that every kindness we manage reflects one we first received. We were saved, Paul writes to Titus, not by the righteous things we had done but according to God's mercy, and the plain note says that a person who remembers what they were before grace found them sees others differently. The God who is gracious and compassionate does not run out, and the kindness he asks of us is drawn from his supply, not from ours.
sit: Who is the person you find hardest to be kind to, and what is one kind thing, safe and wise, you could do for them this week?

prayer.lead: The site's plain note says many people picture God as quick to anger and slow to forgive, and that verse 8 says the opposite, in the words God used to describe himself. Pray it, and ask to become like him.
